official.deadline_note: Two-stage deadline: January 27, 2027 - the high school or cégep submits its Nominee; February 17, 2027 - the Nominee submits the full scholarship application including both reference letters. An admission application to any university listed on the scholarship application must be completed by March 1 of the academic year.
official.application_cycle: 2027 cycle - for students graduating high school or cégep in the 2026/2027 academic year
official.status_note: The official site publishes the 2027 cycle key dates (nomination January 27, 2027; scholarship application February 17, 2027; offers March 8 - June 15, 2027) and links to the live student and high-school nomination application routes.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official wording: 'Schulich Leader Scholarships can devote their full time and attention to their studies, as all of their financial needs are covered over the course of their Bachelor degree.' The page does not use the word 'tuition' separately.
official.funding_period: total award over the degree, paid per academic year
benefits: One hundred scholarships a year across 20 partner universities: half valued at $120,000 for engineering and half valued at $100,000 for science, technology and math.
'Schulich Leader Scholarships can devote their full time and attention to their studies, as all of their financial needs are covered over the course of their Bachelor degree.'
Engineering recipients receive $30,000 and Science, Technology, Math recipients receive $25,000, distributed directly by the university before each academic year.
Entry into a national network of Schulich Leaders plus student enrichment opportunities throughout the year.
No restrictions are set on receiving other awards.
eligibility: Graduating high school or cégep in Canada in the 2026/2027 academic year.
Plan to enrol in an eligible STEM program (science, technology, engineering or math) at one of the 20 partner universities.
Entrepreneurial-minded (exhibiting leadership, charisma and creativity); strong consideration is given to students with financial need.
Intend to pursue a career in technology, engineering, entrepreneurship and business enterprise, or applied scientific research; academic excellence is implied for acceptance into university.

Not considered: students focused on activism (environmental/political/social), intending to become a practising physician or medical researcher, or intending to pursue a career in academia or theoretical research.
requirements: School nomination: every high school in Canada may nominate one graduating student per year (cégeps up to four; a school whose student won in 2026 may nominate two). The nomination form link is available only on request by the school or cégep.

Two referees: contact information is required and referees upload reference letters of no more than one page, addressed to the Schulich Leader Scholarships Selection Committee, received by the February 17, 2027 deadline.

Three required essays (250 words maximum each): what you are passionate about, how you demonstrate an entrepreneurial mindset, and a meaningful risk you took and its outcome; one optional 250-word essay on extenuating circumstances.
Top three achievements, academic or other (50 words maximum each), and a 50-word answer on career aspirations 10 years from now.
The universities you wish to attend must be listed, and an admission application to each listed university must be completed by March 1 of the academic year.
documents: Up-to-date transcript, credit counsel summary or detailed academic report
Two reference letters (one page maximum) submitted by the referees through the emailed online reference request form
selection_criteria: Each of the 20 partner universities selects its own Schulich Leader recipients using its own rubric and adjudication committee.
The programme looks for charismatic future leaders with grit and determination, not necessarily the top academic student in the graduating class.
Financial need: students planning to apply for government assistance for undergraduate study meet the 'Financial Need' criterion.
coverage: 'All of their financial needs are covered over the course of their Bachelor degree' - published programme wording.
$120,000 for engineering or $100,000 for science, technology and math, distributed by the university before each academic year ($30,000 / $25,000 per year).

Funds are non-transferable between universities; the award may be withdrawn if the student fails to pass a year, commits a felony, leaves full-time attendance, or changes away from an eligible STEM area.
application_method: The high school or cégep publicises the opportunity and selects one Schulich Leader Nominee (cégeps may select up to four).
All nominations are verified by the Schulich Leader Scholarships office; the verified Nominee is then emailed a link to the online scholarship application.
The Nominee submits the online application, listing universities and two referees; referees receive an emailed online reference request form after submission and upload their letters.
Each partner university reviews applications and selects its recipients; offers are made between March 8 and June 15, 2027.
official.application_route: School-gated nomination first (no direct or pool applications): the school emails for the nomination form and submits one name by January 27, 2027; only the verified Nominee can then apply online by February 17, 2027.
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian citizen graduating from a high school or cégep in Canada in the 2026/2027 academic year; in Quebec only high schools whose students go directly to university can participate.
official.international_eligibility: International students are not eligible - Canadian citizenship is a published eligibility criterion.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: An eligible STEM program (science, technology, engineering or math) at one of the 20 partner universities; the eligible program list is published per university.
official.description: Schulich Leader Scholarships are Canada's most coveted undergraduate STEM scholarships: one hundred awards a year to entrepreneurial-minded high school graduates enrolling in a science, technology, engineering or math program at 20 partner universities, funded from a $200 million fund launched in 2012 and co-administered by the UJA Federation of Greater Toronto.
official.region: Canada - national programme across 20 partner universities
official.program_type: Private foundation scholarship - undergraduate STEM (funded by the Schulich Foundation, co-administered by UJA Federation of Greater Toronto)

not_confirmed: travel_coverage - no published statement on travel, installation or relocation support
english_requirement - the official pages publish no English language test requirement
research_requirement - no research-proposal requirement is published
verification.notes: Award values ($120,000 engineering / $100,000 science-tech-math), annual distribution amounts, 2027 deadlines, eligibility, application components and selection process were all read directly from the official schulichleaders.com home, apply, FAQ and nominees pages.

applicant_utility.summary: You do not apply yourself - your school nominates you, and the nomination form link is only released to staff on request, so raise it with your guidance counsellor in the autumn rather than in January. Treat February 17, 2027 as your real deadline and note that your two referees only receive their upload link after you submit, so their one-page letters must land the same day. Every university you name must have a completed admission application by March 1, 2027, which means the scholarship and admissions timelines run in parallel.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Canadian citizens in their final year of high school or cégep who have built or led something concrete, can describe a real risk they took, and need funding to attend any university.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm with your guidance office by early January whether your school has requested the nomination link; if nobody has, email the request yourself (info@uja.schulichleaders.com) - schools with a 2026 winner may nominate two students.
Draft the three 250-word essays and the 50-word achievement and aspiration answers before the nomination window so you only assemble, not compose, under deadline.
Brief both referees early: one page maximum, addressed to the Schulich Leader Scholarships Selection Committee with their contact details, uploaded by February 17, 2027.
Record the one-minute video, prepare a headshot and pull your most recent transcript or credit counsel summary before the application link arrives.
Shortlist partner universities whose eligible STEM programmes you actually want, and get those admission applications moving for March 1.
common_rejection_risks: The school never nominates you - there are no pool applications, so this is the single largest point of failure.
Referee letters arriving after February 17, 2027, especially since the referee's form is only triggered once you submit.
Career intent pointing at medicine, medical research, academia or theoretical research, all of which the FAQ excludes.
Listing a university you have not applied to by March 1, which makes you ineligible at that university.
Essays over 250 words or achievements over 50 words, and slideshow-style videos that run past one minute.
Switching universities after winning - funds are non-transferable, so changing schools means losing the award.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published promise is that all financial needs are covered over the Bachelor degree; travel, relocation, personal extras and ancillary fees are not itemised by the programme, so treat anything outside 'financial needs' as self-funded until the university confirms.
document_audit: Transcript must be up to date - a credit counsel summary or detailed academic report is explicitly acceptable, so an unofficial mid-year printout is not necessarily fatal.
Reference letters must be one page maximum, addressed to the Schulich Leader Scholarships Selection Committee and include referee contact information.
The one-minute video and headshot are required uploads, not optional extras.
Word limits are hard: 250 words per essay (plus the optional one) and 50 words per achievement and for the career-aspiration answer.
alerts: Two deadlines, one gate: January 27, 2027 closes the school nomination and February 17, 2027 closes yours - miss the first and the second never opens.
More than one university can make you an offer, and each offer can carry an acceptance deadline set by that university.
Maintenance conditions are strict: pass each year of full-time study, stay in an eligible STEM field and keep a clean record or the university may withdraw the award.
Deferral is possible for up to one academic year but is subject to each university's own policy, so confirm before accepting an offer elsewhere.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: School requests and submits the nomination by January 27, 2027; the programme office verifies it and emails the student a link; the student completes the application and nominates two referees, who upload letters by February 17, 2027; each partner university adjudicates separately and makes offers between March 8 and June 15, 2027.

official.deadline_note: December 1, 2026 is simultaneously the scholarship application deadline, the final document deadline, and the last date for receipt and payment of the direct-entry admission application; decisions are released mid-March 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2027/28 (Fall 2027 direct entry) - the official page states the application is now open
official.status_note: Official wording: 'The application for the 2027/28 International Excellence Entrance Scholarship is now open. Complete application and all required documentation must be received by December 1.' The programme portal lists the award under Fall 2027, Direct Entry - International.
benefits: One award valued at $25,000 and two awards valued at $10,000 each, given to three exceptional international high school graduates each year.
Recognises students who 'combine outstanding leadership potential with academic giftedness' - a named distinction separate from the admission decision.
Short-listed applicants are ranked into first, second and third place based on the results from the award application and the admissions application.
eligibility: Are international students applying directly from high school (direct entry).
Enrolled full-time (minimum 80% course load) in the first year of study in University 1 or any faculty, college or school at the University of Manitoba with a direct entry option.

$25,000 award: minimum admission average of 90% across five of the following senior level high school courses - Math, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Sciences, English, First Language Literature, Geography, History, Music and Visual Arts.
$10,000 awards: achieved the minimum admission requirements for University 1 or any faculty, college or school with a direct entry option.
Have demonstrated strong leadership qualities and sustained, meaningful community involvement.
Have completed a University of Manitoba application for admission by December 1st, including payment of the application fee.
requirements: Submit the separate scholarship application in the University of Manitoba application portal; applications are not considered received until the application is submitted and the non-refundable application fee has been paid by the posted deadline.
Provide one letter of recommendation from a recommender who is either a current teacher or principal, translated into English if required.
Recommender details are required by December 1, 2026 and the recommender's submission must be completed by the same date; referees cannot be family members.
Provide an official interim senior-level (or equivalent) high school transcript by December 1, 2026.
Maintain a full-time course load of at least 80% in the first year of a direct-entry program.
documents: Completed International Excellence Entrance Scholarship application (separate from the admission application)
Official interim senior-level high school transcript or equivalent
One letter of recommendation from a current teacher or principal, translated into English if required
Completed University of Manitoba direct-entry admission application with the application fee paid by December 1, 2026
selection_criteria: Short-listed applicants are ranked into first, second and third place based on the results from the award application and the admissions application.
Outstanding leadership potential and academic giftedness, including sustained, meaningful community involvement.
The 90% five-course average decides the $25,000 place; meeting the minimum admission requirements suffices for the two $10,000 places.
coverage: Cash award of $25,000 (first place) or $10,000 each (second and third place); the official pages publish the award value only and make no statement about tuition, living costs or travel.
application_method: Complete the University of Manitoba direct-entry admission application and pay the application fee by December 1, 2026.
Start or continue the scholarship application in the University of Manitoba application portal under International Excellence Entrance Scholarship - Fall 2027.
Nominate one recommender (current teacher or principal) and ensure their recommendation is submitted by December 1, 2026.
Upload the official interim senior-level transcript; decisions are released by email and posted to the application portal in mid-March 2027.
official.application_route: Two submissions in the University of Manitoba application portal: a direct-entry admission application with the fee paid by December 1, 2026, plus the separate scholarship application with one teacher or principal reference and an interim transcript.
official.study_mode: full-time (minimum 80% course load) in the first year of study
official.citizenship_residency: International students only - the award is designated for exceptional international high school graduates entering directly from high school.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the award is exclusively for international students.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: University 1 or any faculty, college or school at the University of Manitoba with a direct entry option; there is no field-of-study restriction, though the 90% average is calculated across five of the listed senior-level academic courses.
official.duration: Entrance award for the first year of study (students entering September 2027)
official.description: Designed to recognise and encourage exceptional international students applying directly from high school, the University of Manitoba's International Excellence Entrance Scholarship awards one scholarship valued at $25,000 and two valued at $10,000 each to international undergraduates who combine outstanding leadership potential with academic giftedness.
official.region: North America - University of Manitoba, Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada
official.program_type: University merit entrance scholarship (international, direct entry)
official.english_requirement: No English test requirement is published on the scholarship page; the University of Manitoba's university-wide undergraduate English language proficiency standard applies for admission - IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each of the four modules, or approved alternatives (PTE 58, CAEL 60, Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 180, Duolingo 120 with 105 per component, or IAEP Level 5), with results valid at the start of the admission term.

not_confirmed: living_cost_coverage - no published wording about living or personal costs
tuition_coverage - the official pages make no tuition-related statement for this award
payment or disbursement schedule of the award value (instalment vs single payment) is not published
verification.notes: Award values, the 2027/28 cycle wording, the December 1, 2026 deadline, required documents, ranking method and Fall 2027 entry were verified on the University of Manitoba awards page and its official apply.umanitoba.ca programme-information portal; the English standard comes from UM's official English language proficiency requirements page.

applicant_utility.summary: Only three awards exist and the top one needs a 90% average across five specified senior courses, so this is a narrow, top-of-class competition rather than a broad entrance award. Your December 1 checklist has three independent moving parts: the admission application with fee paid, the separate scholarship application, and a teacher or principal who actually submits by the same date. Decisions arrive mid-March 2027, which gives you a funding answer well before most housing and deposit commitments for September 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International high school graduates with a 90%+ five-course average and a documented record of leadership and sustained community involvement, entering University 1 or a direct-entry faculty at Manitoba.
application_readiness_checklist: Pay the admission application fee early - the portal states the application is not received until it is submitted and the non-refundable fee is paid by December 1, 2026.
Request the teacher or principal reference at least three weeks before December 1 and confirm they are not a family member and can speak to sustained community involvement.
Obtain an official interim senior-level transcript now and check that the five courses counted toward the 90% average are all listed.
Open the scholarship application inside the same UM portal as the admission application so both share one deadline and one document upload area.
Use an email address that accepts mail from umanitoba.ca and check the portal around deadlines - all correspondence and decision notices come through both.
common_rejection_risks: Recommender details incomplete or the recommendation not submitted by December 1, 2026 - the onus is explicitly on the applicant.
Unpaid admission application fee, which voids both the admission application and the scholarship application.
Falling short of 90% across five of the listed senior courses, which removes you from the $25,000 tier entirely.
Leadership asserted but not evidenced as sustained, meaningful community involvement in the award and admissions applications.
Registering below a full 80% course load in the first year, which breaks the published full-time condition.
Assuming the general entrance award pool covers this award instead of filing the separate application.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, living costs and travel are not covered by any published wording - this is a cash award of $25,000 or $10,000, so budget separately for international tuition, University Health Insurance, housing in Winnipeg and flights.
document_audit: The recommendation must come from a current teacher or principal, never a family member, and must be translated into English if issued in another language.
The transcript required is an official interim senior-level transcript or equivalent, not a mid-term progress report.
The award application and the admission application are two separate submissions in the same portal - completing one does not complete the other.
Documents must arrive by December 1, 2026 - the portal lists this as a final document deadline, not a start date.
alerts: One date closes everything: application, final documents and admission fee all stop on December 1, 2026, and there is no separate late document window.
Ranking is relative - your award application is read together with your admissions application, so weak admissions materials cap a strong award application.
Apply separately from UM's other entrance awards, which are listed on the Financial Aid and Awards page and are not part of this application.
If offered admission you must accept by the deadline in the offer letter or the offer lapses.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application with fee paid, scholarship application, teacher or principal reference and interim transcript are all filed through the University of Manitoba application portal by December 1, 2026; short-listed applicants are ranked first to third and decisions are released by email and portal in mid-March 2027.
